text:
maya: Quick PR to add a tenant-affinity example for Dedicated provisioning + an SDK snippet. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3421

maya: Key asks: clarify affinity vs autoscale, show YAML + python SDK, and add a tiny migration note for teams on old reserved_pool API.

tom: Nice. Please call out how affinity affects autoscale/burst — cooldown, preemption behavior, and what happens during surge. One-liner is fine.

sasha: Also watch naming: we usually use 'tenant_selector' not 'tenant_label' elsewhere. Consistency is important for copy/paste.

maya: Good catch. I'll standardize to tenant_selector and update examples.

ben: For snippets, I'd like both a curl minimal example and a python SDK sample. I can add the python one if you want the curl to remain tiny.

maya: Please add python. I'll keep curl as a one-liner.

docs-bot: PR #3421 opened by maya — review requested @tom @sasha (https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3421)

sasha: Quick review done. Left a comment on the Isolation section: current wording implies preemption always removes SLA. Suggest: 'may affect latency under reserve pressure' to be less categorical.

tom: Agree with sasha. Also we need to standardize metric names in examples — is it dedicated.capacity.utilization or dedicated.pool.utilization? We should use the canonical one from metric-glossary.

maya: Switched to dedicated.pool.utilization per the glossary and updated the monitoring snippet.

ben: SDK snippet suggestion: create_dedicated_pool(name, model, affinity={"type":"tenant","selector":"team:payments"}, cooldown=300, burst=True). Show expected defaults in a comment.

maya: Added that exact python snippet and a short comment about cooldown default 300s and burst behavior.

maya: Also added a small migration note: teams using the legacy reserved_pool API should map reserved_pool->dedicated_pool and remove the preemptible flag; behavior is handled by scale policies now.

tom: Can we include a quick verification command? e.g. ./tools/provision-sim.sh --config examples/tenant-affinity.yaml and paste expected output. That helps reviewers validate examples quickly.

maya: Added the command and an abbreviated expected output block.

sasha: LGTM pending one more link fix — the autoscale-policy anchor 404s on staging.

maya: Fixed the anchor id and pushed.

ben: I'll follow up with a second PR adding python auth examples (API key vs OIDC flows) for the same snippet.

maya: Fine by me. One more thing: can someone approve legal-friendly SLA phrasing? I suggested: 'SLA is not affected by soft isolation until capacity is actively preempting dedicated pools.' Need sign-off.

tom: I'll do a light wording pass for legal this afternoon.

sasha: Could we also add a tiny ASCII routing diagram? client -> control-plane -> dedicated-pool -> model-shard. Helps non-engineers.

maya: Added a small ASCII diagram and a single-sentence explanation of routing + fallback.

deploy-bot: docs CI: all checks passed for PR #3421 — staging build: https://staging.docs.redwood.ai/tenant-affinity

maya: Merged after CI passed. Thanks everyone :tada:

tom: Great. Can we create an examples/tenancy/README.md to collect these snippets?

maya: Filed ticket #5687 to track the README and the follow-up python auth examples.

ben: Closing loop — will open follow-up PR for auth examples.

maya: Closing the thread here. Thanks for the quick reviews and the link fixes!
